cim: Inside the biggest feud in artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: Inside the biggest feud in artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
Being in San Francisco in the mid-2020s sometimes feels like what I imagine living in Los Alamos was like in 1943 when the Manhattan Project rolled into town. The air is heavy with excitement and dread. Engineers toil, day and night, on systems of profound consequence. Wild-eyed prophets sell visions of a transformed world, and politicians drop in to check on the progress of the project. ­Everyone knows that the fates of nations, and trillions of dollars of capital, rely on what happens here, yet no one can fully appreciate what it would mean if the project succeeds.

One person consumed by this question is Dario Amodei, a Princeton-educated physicist who left Google in 2016 to join OpenAI, then a fledgling non-profit artificial intelligence research lab. He looked the part of a mad scientist, with round glasses and short brown ringlets that he twisted in his fingers whenever he was feeling nervous or thinking hard about something. He was known among his colleagues as a brilliant, bullheaded researcher with deep convictions about AI, which he often expressed by writing long essays that he circulated within the company.
